questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another vehicle). Use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see. Wear reflective materials to be more visible. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and stay safe. Do not stay only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.question: During the day, you should use your headlight on:

options.text: Alternating between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. This helps other drivers see you. Use high beam whenever you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases the risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars to avoid the center. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have rounded, or convex, mirrors. What do these mirrors do?

options.text: Are easy to adjust to immediately.
Make cars look closer than they are.
Show a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to convex mirrors.

questions.question: If your front wheel begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately, then re-engage it.
Release the front brake and increase rear brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-engage it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely and immediately. Then reapply it smoothly.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that another driver sees you. Always assume that any vehicle that could enter your path will. Stay alert and ride defensively.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or place them in saddlebags. Do not stack loads on the back of the seat or sissy bar because this raises the center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle next to a curb, how should it be positioned?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: To work properly, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Stop all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist breaks, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: If you brake while turning in a curve:

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do it carefully. Your tires are already using traction to make the turn while leaning, so less traction is left for stopping.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: How many motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: Who should control the speed in a group of riders?
questions.explanation: The last rider in a group should control the speed. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: If you ride a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, you should ride in a:
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles normally ride in a staggered formation, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. Three-wheel motorcycle groups should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Always ride in the same spot in the lane.
Change position in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on the current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle hits you with a wind blast, you have the most room to recover if you are riding:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most space to recover if a wind blast from a passing vehicle affects your control.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week. This is part of basic motorcycle safety checks.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright and let the motorcycle lean into the turn.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These signs tell you the rules of the road.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the middle of each lane. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride only on it because it has more traction.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil builds up in the center of lanes from vehicles. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough traction. When wet, avoid it. The oily strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it while staying in the center of your lane.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They never need to be replaced.
They get scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
They should be made of breakable materials so they break in a crash.
They should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. They scratch and become brittle as they age. Replace them often for the best protection.
